summary: A sound IELTS paper: a lost-property call with phone number and spelling, a volunteer briefing with a matching box, a two-student design discussion and a full lecture on beavers. All keys are correct and every answer is heard in question order.
strengths: Part 1 traps: 35 vs 53, Tuesday corrected to Wednesday, black denied for grey, the central-station office closed, five thousand raised to ten.
Part 2 MCQs each reject two options with reasons (postponed second stage, posted T-shirts that went missing, first-aid tent kept for emergencies).
Part 3 eliminates options clearly and naturally (station vs museum vs market; 1:50 too big, 1:200 too small; cardboard warps, balsa too dear).
Part 4 notes paraphrase the lecture well ("block a stream" for "drags branches into the current", "slow the water down" for "acts as a brake").

issues.problem: Part 1 script is 486 words, short for a full Part 1 (very roughly 600+).
issues.change: If re-recorded, add an exchange about the time of the journey or a second contact number.

issues.problem: In the Part 2 box, the two unused options ("is the most popular choice", "is only for returning volunteers") are never mentioned, so they are easy to cross out.
issues.change: Replace them with near misses the script touches, e.g. "involves working with children" (the children's area volunteers only assist) or "starts after the gates open".

issues.problem: Several items are heard word for word with little paraphrase (Q14 "tell your team leader", Q24 "foam board", Q28 "the glass roof", Q30 "update the diary").
issues.change: Reword options, e.g. Q30 "bring the project log up to date".
